faq.question: What does Salih mean?
faq.answer: Salih is associated with the Arabic form صَالِح, whose core sense is salih; righteous; a prophet.

faq.question: What is the origin of Salih?
faq.answer: Salih is associated with Arabic. Salih is Arabic صَالِح (Ṣāliḥ), meaning 'righteous'; it is the name of a prophet in the Quran.

faq.question: Is Salih an Arabic name?
faq.answer: Yes — the underlying form صَالِح is Arabic.

faq.question: Is Salih an Islamic name?
faq.answer: Salih can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.answer: Salih should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ṣāliḥ occurs in the Quran as the name of a prophet.
